title: Recognised for work reducing health inequalities in the early years
excerpt: Our programme development work addressing health inequalities for babies, children and young people has been recognised as good practice across North-West London.
coverAlt: Two young girls sit together writing and drawing at a desk
body: We're glad to share that strategic programme development work we led to address health inequalities for babies, children and young people within a London borough has been recognised as good practice across North-West London, through the Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) assessment focused on asthma prevention and care.

The programme itself was never about asthma in isolation. It was built on the same premise that underpins most of our work: that the conditions shaping a child's health outcomes are set long before any single diagnosis, in housing, in air quality, in how early the right support reaches a family, and in whether services are joined up enough to notice a child falling through the gaps.

Recognition like this matters less as an endpoint and more as a signal — evidence that when local systems commit to genuinely co-designed, equity-focused delivery, it's visible in outcomes that reach well beyond the programme's original brief.
We're grateful to the local authority, NHS and community partners who made this work possible, and to the families whose experience shaped it from the start.
